primitives.name: Entity Tracking Schema
primitives.verbatim_quote: The entity-schema design and the event/stint extraction pipeline are a reusable template for GSE's own NGS tracking-data store and feature extraction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time step (dimensionless)', 'E_i': 'entity identifier (integer)', 'x_i(t)': 'x-coordinate (meters)', 'y_i(t)': 'y-coordinate (meters)', 'z_i(t)': 'z-coordinate (meters)', 'v_i(t)': 'velocity magnitude (m/s)', 'team_i': 'team affiliation (binary or categorical)', 'role_i': 'position type (discrete, 8 categories)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each entity has a center-of-mass trajectory; discrete roles capture team structure; no pose estimation included.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When entity tracking fails due to occlusion or missing positional data.

primitives.name: Event Extraction Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Event extraction:** rule-based from raw tracking — passes/receptions (possession transfer to teammate), turnovers/interceptions (to opponent), shots (ball moved in attacking direction + goal / out beyond goal line / to opposing keeper).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{pass}': 'pass event timestamp (seconds)', 'T_{shot}': 'shot event timestamp (seconds)', 'T_{turnover}': 'turnover/interception timestamp (seconds)', 'possession_i(t)': 'boolean flag indicating possession (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rule-based logic approximates real-world event definitions; possession tracking is accurate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession flags are mislabeled or event boundaries are ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Derives structured play events from raw entity trajectories for downstream analytics.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of event classification against ground-truth annotations.

primitives.name: Stint Segmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Stint identification:** automatic segmentation of continuous gameplay with unique IDs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_j': 'stint identifier (integer)', 't_start_j': 'start time of stint (seconds)', 't_end_j': 'end time of stint (seconds)', 'duration_j': 'duration of stint (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Continuous gameplay segments are well-defined by temporal coherence of events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When game state transitions are abrupt or event boundaries are unclear.

layer2.mapping: Segments gameplay into coherent units for temporal modeling and feature engineering.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal continuity of stint boundaries validated via event sequence alignment.

The core innovation lies in mapping simulated environments to real-world sports analytics through a reusable schema. The entity-tracking schema encodes agent states as rows in a relational table, enabling structured querying and aggregation. Event extraction applies deterministic rules to infer high-level actions from low-level motion data. Stint segmentation provides temporal granularity for longitudinal analysis. These primitives form a closed-loop system where simulated data can be used to develop and test models before deployment on real tracking data. The failure mode occurs when the simulation does not accurately reflect real-world dynamics, particularly in complex interactions or rare events. The mathematical duality is between discrete state evolution and continuous event occurrence, bridging the gap between reinforcement learning and sports analytics.
